subject: Throughput validation & observability asks for ShipMate pilot
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@shipmate.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: throughput & streaming needs (ShipMate pilot)

Alex —

Thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap & the asks we captured on the call so we can align the pilot sizing and SLOs. Happy to iterate if I missed anything.

High-level goals you mentioned:
- Pilot target: 10k DAU generating ~1.2M tokens/day (estimate you shared)
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 350ms for short assistant responses (<128 tokens); 95th <= 700ms for longer generations (~512 tokens)
- Streaming: customers expect first-token streaming for conversational UI (partial tokens delivered within 150–200ms)
- Peak vs steady: 3x peak multiplier on top of steady-state during promo windows, with 60–90s peak windows
- Cost sensitivity: prefer quantized variants if accuracy loss <2% on prompt set

Sizing & observability asks (what we need from you to validate sizing):
1) Representative traffic extract (CSV) with timestamp, prompt token count, response token count, and spike markers (sample attached format)
2) Typical prompt examples (10–20) including multi-turn back-and-forths and any streaming-dependent prompts
3) Expected concurrency (number of simultaneous active chat sessions) and if you use long-lived connections for streaming
4) Peak windows definition (how often, typical duration)
5) Any on-prem or VPC/network constraints that could impact RTT

Next steps (proposed):
- You: share traffic extract + representative prompts (attach to this thread) — target EOD tomorrow
- Us: run a quick profiling pass (tokens/sec, concurrency simulation) and return a short sizing spreadsheet with recommended config (GPU type, batch knobs, cache settings) — within 48 hours of receiving traces
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with infra & streaming engineer (30–45m) to validate streaming handshake and fallback behavior (we can do Mon/Tue next week)

Attachments: call-recording-20270818.mp4 (recording), initial-sizing-estimate-shipmate.xlsx (skeleton)

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@shipmate.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@shipmate.io>
Date: 2027-08-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & streaming needs (ShipMate pilot)

Rafael, Neha, Ben —

Appreciate the clear recap. Attached is a first-pass extract: shipmate_traffic_extract_202708.csv. A few clarifications inline:

- The 1.2M tokens/day is our current conservative estimate; if Q3 campaign runs we expect short spikes up to ~4x for 10–20 minutes.
- Typical prompt size: median 34 tokens, 90th 180 tokens; responses med 48 tokens, 90th 320 tokens.
- Concurrency: we expect 1200 active chat sessions during steady state, peaks to 4800 concurrently during campaign bursts.
- Streaming: we do use a long-lived SSE connection; client expects a first-byte within 150ms and steady token updates every 60–80ms after the first byte.
- Security: we need data-at-rest to be isolated for pilot; happy to discuss Private deployment later but start with Dedicated.

I'll attach the CSV now; procurement copied for contract cadence. Let me know available times for the deep-dive next week (prefer morning PST).

— Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Product
ShipMate
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-18T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & streaming needs (ShipMate pilot)

Nice notes. A couple immediate internal items:
- I will run a quick token-velocity profile from the CSV and produce a peak-window heatmap (expect results in ~24 hrs).
- We should validate streaming latency under head-of-line (HoL) conditions — I'll spin up a small harness that simulates 5k concurrent SSE clients and measure first-byte and per-token gaps.
- Ben: can you look at the security ask (data-at-rest isolation) and pull in infra for Dedicated pricing delta?

If Alex is good with Mon morning PST, I can join the deep-dive with a short readout of the profile.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Performance & SLOs, Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@shipmate.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@shipmate.io>
Date: 2027-08-20T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & streaming needs (ShipMate pilot)

Alex —

Thanks for the CSV and clarifications — that's perfect. Neha and the team will send the heatmap and a short sizing sheet by EOD tomorrow.

Proposed deep-dive: Monday 2027-08-23 at 10:00am PST — 45 minutes. Agenda:
1) Traffic heatmap & peak-window definition (Neha)
2) Streaming handshake and first-byte expectations (infra/streaming eng)
3) Sizing recommendation + Dedicated delta (Ben)
4) Data isolation approach & timeline (security)

Action items for ShipMate:
- Share any additional prompt examples (especially multi-turn flows)
- Confirm whether the campaign spikes are forecasted (dates) or event-driven
- Provide an AWS account/project ID (read-only) if you prefer we run a short test using your staging environment (optional)

I'll send a calendar invite and drop the Drive link for artifacts. Thanks again — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Rafael
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
